Around the Geospatial, 3D, and AEC Industries: Ancient Structures, Coastlines, and Digital Twins

2026-08-24 Abigail Hart, Geo Week News lidar, Amazon rainforest, ancient civilization, coastline mapping, flooding, erosion, digital twins, 3D printing, geospatial industry, AEC
Read the source article

Quick summary

Geo Week News rounds up three standout geospatial stories: lidar revealing 24,000–30,000 ancient earthworks in the Amazon, a 5,000 km Australian coastline hazard assessment, and how 3D printing is transforming digital twin creation for the AEC industry.

Key takeaways

  • Airborne lidar has revealed a previously unknown "Aquiry civilization" in Brazil's Acre state with 24,000–30,000 monumental earthworks
  • Researchers estimate 1.25–3 million people lived in the Amazon region in the first centuries AD — more densely populated than today
  • Engineering firm Hatch completed a first-of-its-kind digital mapping assessment of 5,000 km of Australian coastline for flooding and erosion risk
  • 1.4 million Australian properties are already at risk of flooding, with annual event costs approaching $400 million
  • The coastline assessment used statistical and process-based modelling for a state government agency to create a consistent region-wide hazard picture
  • The third story explores how 3D printing technology is being used to create physical models from digital twin data in the AEC industry
  • The roundup demonstrates the breadth of geospatial applications from archaeology to coastal engineering to construction
